4:Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5:-/
6:import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiCompact
7:import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UnderlyingMap
8:
9:/-!
10:# DJ-0: quasi-compactness from a compact-space source via a surjection
11:
12:The smallest, ungated brick of the DAT-J worksheet (`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
13:§2.4): the abstract topological shape that `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes to get
14:quasi-compactness of the Jacobian structure morphism from the Abel image of `Div^g`-lite.
15:
16:The mathematics is entirely mathlib's: the continuous surjective image of a compact space
17:is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). This file packages that for scheme
18:morphisms and adds the quasi-compactness corollary over an affine base, so DAT-J's qc
19:field is a one-line instantiation. It is deliberately **Challenge-free** (mathlib-only, no
20:curve/Challenge imports) — the DAT-J producer cone must not cycle through `Challenge.lean`
21:(worksheet §0.5 / risk 1).
22:
23:## Main results
24:
25:* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_surjective`: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of
26:  schemes out of a compact-space source `X`, then `Y` is a compact space.
27:* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective`: a structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an
28:  affine base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives such a surjection. This is the
29:  shape DAT-J's DJ-1 consumes with `X := Div^g` (`compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel`
30:  the Abel morphism, `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`.
31:-/
32:
33:set_option autoImplicit false
34:
35:universe u
36:
37:open CategoryTheory
38:
39:namespace AlgebraicGeometry
40:
41:variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
42:
43:/-- **DJ-0, compact-image half.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of schemes out of a
44:compact-space source, then the target is a compact space: the underlying map of `f` is a
45:continuous surjection (`Scheme.Hom.continuous`), and the continuous surjective image of a
46:compact space is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). -/
47:theorem compactSpace_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace X]
48:    (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : CompactSpace Y :=
49:  hf.compactSpace f.continuous
50:
51:/-- **DJ-0, quasi-compactness corollary.** A structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an affine
52:base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives a surjection `f : X ⟶ Y` from a
53:compact-space source `X`. Over an affine base, `QuasiCompact g` is exactly `CompactSpace Y`
54:(`HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine`, the `DivSchemeQProj` pattern), which the
55:compact-image half supplies.
56:
57:This is the abstract shape `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes: instantiate
58:`X := Div^g` (compact via `compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel` the Abel morphism
59:(surjective on points, DJ-1), `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`. -/
60:theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsAffine Z]
61:    [CompactSpace X] (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : QuasiCompact g :=
62:  haveI : CompactSpace Y := compactSpace_of_surjective f hf
63:  HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
64:
65:end AlgebraicGeometry

30:**What this is and is not.**  It is the plumbing of §2.2 steps 1, 2 and 4, discharged once.
31:Step 3 — surjectivity of the Abel map on points — is DJ-1's honest brick and is *not* proved
32:here.  Per §0.5 that brick must stay Challenge-free: use `exists_effective_of_picClass` /
33:`riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`.
34:
35:**AMENDMENT 2026-07-29, two corrections to the sentence this replaces.**  It used to say the
36:brick "needs the universal degree-`g` class, hence `divRep`, plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`
37:and the `fiberTwist` shift".  Both cost claims were wrong:
38:
39:* **Not `divRep`-gated.**  The effectivity content is landed and divRep-free at every point of
40:  any `Pic⁰`-representing object (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`,
41:  `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`).  Only the Abel *square* needs the
42:  representation.
43:* **No `fiberTwist` shift.**  At degree exactly `g` the entry condition `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)`
44:  reads `g ≤ deg W`, so the class sits on the boundary and `exists_effective_of_picClass` fires
45:  with no slack.  A shift is what one needs to lift a degree-*zero* class into the effective
46:  range, and that is one multiplication by a fixed degree-`g` class
47:  (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`), not a `fiberTwist` construction.
48:
49:What genuinely remains on this side is **descent**: the divisor is produced over a finite
50:separable splitting field of `κ(y)`, and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)`.
51:
52:Note that the statements below take the surjection as a *bare morphism* out of `DivScheme g`
53:rather than as an Abel map built from a representation.  That is deliberate: it keeps the
54:file independent of the divisor-representability chain, so the qc mechanism is available to
55:any producer of a surjection — including the chart-atlas route, which does not name an Abel
56:map at all.
57:-/

59:set_option autoImplicit false
60:set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
61:
62:universe u
63:
64:open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
65:
66:namespace AlgebraicGeometry
67:
68:variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
69:variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
70:variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
71:
72:/-! ## The qc step at the campaign's compact source -/
73:
74:section Qc
75:
76:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
77:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
78:variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
79:variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤))
80:variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
81:
82:/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step** (w4-datj §2.2 steps 1, 2, 4): if the Jacobian-to-be
83:receives a point-surjective morphism from the divisor scheme `DivScheme g`, its structure
84:morphism is quasi-compact.
85:
86:`DivScheme g` is a compact space (`compactSpace_divScheme`, DD-Q: it is a closed subscheme of
87:a Grassmannian pair with a finite affine atlas), the base `Spec k` is affine, and DJ-0's
88:`quasiCompact_of_surjective` converts a surjection out of a compact space into
89:quasi-compactness of the structure morphism.
90:
91:So the whole a-posteriori qc argument is reduced to surjectivity — which is DJ-1's honest
92:brick and is not supplied here. -/
93:theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
94:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
95:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
96:    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
97:  quasiCompact_of_surjective abel J.hom hsurj
98:
99:end Qc
100:
101:/-! ## DJ-2: the packaging -/
102:
103:section Package
104:
105:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
106:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
107:variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
108:variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
109:variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
110:
111:/-- **DJ-2, the packaging** (w4-datj §1.1): the pinned Jacobian datum from a representation
112:of the degree-zero Picard functor, its locally-of-finite-type certificate, and a
113:point-surjective morphism from `DivScheme g`.
114:
115:This is `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` with the fourth field replaced by the Abel-image
116:hypothesis, which is the form the classical construction produces: quasi-compactness of the
117:Jacobian is *not* structural (its atlas is infinite, §2.1) and has to come from the image
118:argument. -/
119:noncomputable def JacobianData.ofAbelImage (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
120:    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
121:    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
122:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
123:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
124:    JacobianData C :=
125:  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft
126:    (quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J abel hsurj)
127:
128:@[simp]
129:lemma JacobianData.ofAbelImage_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
130:    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
131:    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
132:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
133:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
134:    (JacobianData.ofAbelImage C J rep hlft abel hsurj).J = J :=
135:  rfl
136:
137:end Package

139:/-! ## The chart-atlas form -/
140:
141:section Charts
142:
143:variable {ι : Type u} {Xc : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144:variable (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (Xc i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
145:variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
146:variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
147:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
148:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
149:variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
150:variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
151:variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
152:
153:/-- **The atlas producer with the qc field discharged by the Abel image**: the infinite-atlas
154:producer `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` asks for `CompactSpace` of the glued object,
155:which §2.1 records as the genuinely a-posteriori input.  This supplies it from a surjection
156:out of `DivScheme g`, so an atlas plus a surjective Abel map is enough — no finiteness of the
157:chart index, which the chart index (one chart per divisor class with an effective witness)
158:does not have. -/
159:noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage
160:    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
161:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left)
162:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
163:    JacobianData C :=
164:  JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft
165:    (compactSpace_of_surjective abel hsurj)
166:
167:end Charts

41:  step from per-point lifts.
42:* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
43:  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
44:  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.
45:
46:## What this does NOT do
47:
48:It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
49:`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
50:§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape
51:of that obligation: a lift *per point*, stated with no reference to `Function.Surjective`,
52:instead of a global surjectivity claim about a topological map.
53:-/

64:/-! ## The conversion: per-point lifts give surjectivity -/
65:
66:section Topology
67:
68:variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
69:
70:/-- **Per-point residue-field lifts give point surjectivity.**  If every point `y` of `Y`
71:admits a morphism `q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ X` with `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then the
72:underlying map of `f` is surjective.
73:
74:`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
75:is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point
76:of `Spec κ(y)` lies in the fibre of `f` over `y`.
77:
78:This is the missing link between what the Picard side produces and what DAT-J's
79:quasi-compactness field consumes: `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields a *morphism* out of
80:a residue field, while `quasiCompact_of_surjective` wants a surjection of topological
81:spaces. -/
82:theorem surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift (f : X ⟶ Y)
83:    (h : ∀ y : Y, ∃ q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X,
84:      q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y) :
85:    Function.Surjective f.base := by
86:  intro y
87:  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := h y
88:  -- a field is nontrivial, so `Spec κ(y)` has a point
89:  obtain ⟨s⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
90:  refine ⟨q.base s, ?_⟩
91:  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]
92:  rw [Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hs
93:  exact hs
94:
95:end Topology

97:/-! ## DJ-1's quasi-compactness step from per-point lifts -/
98:
99:section Qc
100:
101:variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
102:variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
103:  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
104:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
105:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
106:variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
107:variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤))
108:variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
109:
110:/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step, from per-point lifts** (w4-datj §2.2 with step 3 in
111:the shape §2.3 delivers it): if every point of the Jacobian-to-be receives a
112:`DivScheme g`-valued lift of its residue-field point, the structure morphism is
113:quasi-compact.
114:
115:This composes `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` with DJ-0's
116:`quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme`; the compact source is DD-Q's
117:`compactSpace_divScheme` instance, and the base is affine. -/
118:theorem quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme
119:    (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
120:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
121:    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
122:      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
123:      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
124:    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
125:  quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J abel
126:    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)
127:
128:end Qc

130:/-! ## The `JacobianData` producers -/
131:
132:section Package
133:
134:variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
135:variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
136:  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
137:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
138:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
139:variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
140:variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
141:variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
142:
143:/-- **DJ-2 against per-point lifts**: the pinned Jacobian datum from a representation of
144:the degree-zero Picard functor, its locally-of-finite-type certificate, and a
145:`DivScheme g`-valued lift of every residue-field point of `J.left`.
146:
147:`JacobianData.ofAbelImage` asks for `Function.Surjective abel.base`; this asks for the
148:per-point lifts the classical argument produces, which is the same input one step earlier. -/
149:noncomputable def JacobianData.ofAbelLifts (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
150:    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
151:    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
152:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
153:    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
154:      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
155:      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
156:    JacobianData C :=
157:  JacobianData.ofAbelImage C J rep hlft abel
158:    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)
159:
160:@[simp]
161:lemma JacobianData.ofAbelLifts_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
162:    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
163:    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
164:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
165:    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
166:      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
167:      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
168:    (JacobianData.ofAbelLifts C J rep hlft abel hlift).J = J :=
169:  rfl
170:
171:end Package

173:/-! ## The chart-atlas form -/
174:
175:section Charts
176:
177:variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178:variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
179:  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
180:variable {ι : Type u} {Xc : ι → Scheme.{u}}
181:variable (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (Xc i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
182:variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
183:variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
184:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
185:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
186:variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
187:variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
188:variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
189:
190:/-- **The atlas producer against per-point lifts** — the one critical-path §7.5 needs, since
191:the chart index is infinite and `CompactSpace` of the glued object is genuinely
192:a-posteriori.  Per-point residue-field lifts of the Abel morphism supply it. -/
193:noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts
194:    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
195:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left)
196:    (hlift : ∀ y : (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left,
197:      ∃ q : Spec ((gluedOfCharts C f hf).left.residueField y) ⟶
198:        DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
199:        q ≫ abel = (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
200:    JacobianData C :=
201:  JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage C f hf hlft abel
202:    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)
203:
204:end Charts

206:end AlgebraicGeometry
